claims.statement: Zero Share is a fully serverless static frontend: Astro builds with output 'static' mounting Svelte components client:only, with a service-worker integration for PWA support, and no server-side runtime or relay exists anywhere in the app.

The '/' route renders the OfferPage (initiator role) and '/receive' renders the ReceivePage (responder role); each Astro page is a thin wrapper mounting one Svelte component under the shared MainLayout.
After the data channel opens, both pages mount both a Sender and a Receiver with a Send/Receive toggle, so either peer can transfer files in either direction over the same channel.

Peer connections are configured with a single ICE server (default stun:stun.l.google.com:19302) resolved through the shared isSupportedIceServer/resolveIceServer predicates in src/configs.ts, which accept the built-in STUN allowlist plus any well-formed stun:/turns: URL; the sender enforces the predicate on both the emitted `i` link param and its own RTCPeerConnection and the receiver enforces the same predicate on the accepted `i` param, so a custom/TURN server chosen on the sender is always honored and the two peers can never diverge; anything else falls back to the default with an error toast on both sides, and no relay server exists.

Offer establishment mints the RSA keypair exactly once at the top of generateOfferLink (before the peer exists), creates the RTCPeerConnection with a data channel (ordered:false) using the predicate-resolved ICE server, generates the local offer, then waits for ICE candidates to finish or a 3-second timeout (WAIT_ICE_CANDIDATES_TIMEOUT) before building the offer link; a per-invocation offerBuilt flag claims the build synchronously so the two paths build the link at most once and the timeout fallback can never rotate the key. Regeneration is generation-safe: before minting, generateOfferLink clears the pending ICE-candidate timer, nulls the handlers and closes the old data channel and RTCPeerConnection (unless already closed), resets the settled peer crypto (rsaPub to undefined, effectiveEncrypt re-pinned from the live setting) and the dead generation's UI state (new-file badge, isConnecting, pending answer code, and the dead generation's offer link so a failed regeneration returns to the clean generate state with no dead link to copy/QR/accept), and bumps a monotonically increasing offerGeneration token; the timeout fallback re-checks that token at fire time so a stale timer holding the previous generation's public key can never build a link from the new peer's SDP. Synchronous construction/offer-creation failures (a rejected createOffer()/setLocalDescription() or a synchronous constructor throw) are caught, toasted, and — since PR #108 — the just-created generation is torn down with the same guarded shape as the regeneration teardown: the pending ICE-candidate timer is cleared, the new data channel's four handlers are nulled before dataChannel.close() and the variable reset to undefined, and the new RTCPeerConnection is closed guarded on connectionState !== 'closed' (when the failure happened before the peer/channel existed both guards skip) — otherwise the failed peer's ICE agent, UDP sockets, and STUN/TURN keepalives would leak until the next generation or page unload. Since PR #135 the two channel-death handlers no longer carry a local guarded close (their peer release moved into the shared createChannelTeardown() helper), so the offer page now has TWO local guarded connection.close() call sites — the regeneration teardown and the offer-creation catch — and tests/dead-channel-peer-close.test.mjs pins that the offer page closes the peer in exactly those two places and never inside a death handler, while ReceivePage locally never closes the peer.

The answer peer decodes the attacker-controllable `s` URL param via sdpDecode (which throws synchronously on empty, invalid-base64, or non-SDP input) inside a try/catch that surfaces an 'Invalid SDP in link' toast instead of crashing the page during load (PR #45); the setOfferSDP promise is kept and awaited before createAnswer with a signalingState === 'have-remote-offer' check, so a rejected setRemoteDescription flips offerFailed and the UI renders an error state ('offer in the link is invalid') instead of the spinner spinning forever; it then awaits the validated p-param key import (a malformed key downgrades the session to plaintext) and produces the answer code sdpEncode(answerSdp) + '|' + base64(RSA public key) with the same 3-second ICE candidate timeout fallback.

All data-channel traffic is proto3-framed Message bytes: a file id plus exactly one of metaData (name, size, type, encrypted AES key), chunk (file body slice), or receiveEvent (receiver control event); there is no ad-hoc text protocol on the channel.

Both pages dispatch incoming data-channel messages through the shared handlePeerMessage helper in src/utils/peerMessage.ts (deduplicated from the two identical per-page handlers in PR #71): the same oneof switch (metaData routes to Receiver.onMetaData, chunk to Receiver.onChunkData, receiveEvent to Sender.onReceiveEvent), with Message.decode on the peer-controlled bytes wrapped in try/catch inside the helper so a malformed/truncated protobuf frame drops the frame and toasts 'Invalid message from peer' instead of crashing the page uncaught (PR #46). Both pages pin dataChannel.binaryType = 'arraybuffer' at channel acquisition (offer side at the createDataChannel site; answer side at the ondatachannel site) because WebRTC's default 'blob' would make new Uint8Array(Blob) zero-length and silently drop every frame (PR #95). Both pages additionally wire the data channel's onerror/onclose to the shared createChannelTeardown() helper's handlers (see the dead-channel teardown claim), which propagate 'connection lost' into both file pipelines and release the RTCPeerConnection — no page carries its own guarded connection.close() inside a death handler since PR #135. tests/dead-channel-peer-close.test.mjs and tests/peer-message-handler.test.mjs statically pin the dispatch, the binaryType pin, and the shared-teardown wiring.

The file transfer protocol is receiver-ack chunking: the sender emits metaData, waits for EVENT_RECEIVER_ACCEPT, then sends one chunk per EVENT_RECEIVED_CHUNK acknowledgment sent by the receiver — a simple backpressure loop pacing the transfer.

Application-layer encryption is optional and off by default (DEFAULT_SEND_OPTIONS.isEncrypt false): when enabled, each file gets its own AES-256-GCM key wrapped with the receiver's RSA-OAEP-2048 public key, with the wrapped key delivered inside the metaData message, protecting file content from SDP-exchange MITM on top of DTLS; the answer peer awaits the validated p-param import before generating its own RSA pair for the answer code. The offer side tracks the effective session encryption in a plain $state effectiveEncrypt: while no offer link exists, onOptionsUpdate re-syncs it from the live setting and clears the imported peer key; once the link is live the session is settled by the handshake (the accepted answer's key portion pins it — present = encrypted, empty = plaintext), so a post-generation options change (chunk size, ICE server, or encryption toggle) cannot desync Sender/Receiver from the peer's settled mode.

File state lives entirely in client memory as reactive Svelte maps keyed by file id (crypto.randomUUID on the sender side), with per-file progress/bitrate stats kept in non-reactive maps and flushed to UI state every PROGRESS_UPDATE_UI_STEP (3) percentage points to throttle renders; the sender's connectionLost flag is a plain $state that the template reacts to — NOT a $derived(channelSender.isLost()) (a $derived over the helper's isLost() would cache false forever because isLost() reads a plain closure variable, not a Svelte signal) — flipped by onChannelClose() and by a thin send() wrapper mirroring the helper's lost flag (PR #109), while the receiver gates on the helper's isLost() read directly.

The app has no persistence: received files are assembled into an in-memory Blob only when the received byte count exactly matches the declared metaData.size (the completion gate is an exact match, not >=) and downloaded on demand via an object URL (single files and a bulk store-only ZIP export); nothing is stored in IndexedDB, localStorage, or any server.

MetaData.size is int64 on the wire (widened from int32 in commit 721c502 / PR #42), so files of 2 GiB or larger no longer throw 'invalid int32' during Message.encode; tests/protocol-size.test.mjs pins this by encoding and round-tripping 3 GiB and MAX_SAFE_INTEGER sizes through the generated proto code.

The manual-exchange clipboard copy handlers are guarded (PR #79): copyOfferLink on the offer page and copyAnswerCode on the receive page wrap navigator.clipboard.writeText in try/catch, so a rejection (non-secure context, denied permission, unavailable API) toasts a 'Copy failed' error instead of escaping as an unhandled rejection that would let the user believe the link/answer code was copied when it was not.

The guarded data-channel send (dead-channel flag + readyState check + throwing-send catch) is a single shared helper: createChannelSender(dataChannel) in src/utils/channelSender.ts returns { send(message), isLost(), markLost() } — send no-ops with false when the lost flag is set or readyState !== 'open', returns true on success, and on a throwing send flips the lost flag and returns false instead of leaking InvalidStateError; markLost() is the idempotent flip fired by the owning component's onChannelClose(); isLost() is the helper's live read. Sender.svelte and Receiver.svelte each create one instance; the sender keeps its plain send(...) call-site shape through a thin wrapper that calls the helper's send and mirrors the helper's lost flag into its UI $state, so the pipeline guard and the UI gate share one source of truth (PR #97 dedup, PR #109 UI flag).

acceptAnswer refuses to signal a dead peer (PR #104): before parsing the pasted/scanned answer code it checks connection and connectionState — if the channel's onerror/onclose handler already closed the RTCPeerConnection (or a racing regeneration did), it toasts 'Connection lost — generate a new offer to connect' and returns, instead of applying the answer to a closed peer, which would only fail inside the setRemoteDescription try/catch with a misleading 'Invalid answer code'.

onAccept bails on a combined null + status guard before the ACCEPT send — `if (!receivingFile || receivingFile.status !== FileStatus.WaitingAccept) return;` (PR #117): a second Accept click that lands in the same frame as the first (before Svelte re-renders the button away) previously passed the bare null guard and sent a second EVENT_RECEIVER_ACCEPT, re-initializing the per-file chunk/stats maps and deleting the chunkQueue entry; the sender's persistent ACCEPT handler then fired sendNextChunk() concurrently, the same chunk went on the wire twice, receivedSize double-counted, and the receiver marked a fully-delivered file Success or rejected it as oversized via rejectOversizedStream. The same guard also covers entries that onChannelClose already bounced to Pending (+error), where re-accepting would re-initialize chunk state for a file that can never complete. The guard runs before, and does not short-circuit, the metadata-failure reject branch — a WaitingAccept entry carrying error / a missing aesKey still reaches the PR #78 'Cannot accept ... the metadata/key failed to process' reject path. Pinned by tests/receiver-double-accept.test.mjs: a pre-fix control proving the double click sends two EVENT_RECEIVER_ACCEPT, a post-fix no-op proof (exactly one ACCEPT, chunk map not recreated, a dead-channel Pending entry stays Pending with no ACCEPT sent), a metadata-failure-entry-still-rejects check, and static regex guards that the real onAccept carries the combined null+status guard after the entry capture and before the reject branch.

The receiver bounds peer-driven incoming files against resource exhaustion (PR #131): before registering a new entry, onMetaData counts active (non-Success) entries against MAX_INCOMING_FILES (32) and the total declared size of every not-yet-removed entry against MAX_TOTAL_RECEIVED_BYTES (8 GiB); a frame that would exceed either cap is not registered and is rejected back to the sender with EVENT_RECEIVER_REJECT plus a single error toast, and the frame's own id is excluded from both counts so a re-offer of an already-held file never counts against the caps.

Metadata size is validated to be a positive integer (PR #127): validateFileMetadata rejects a MetaData.size that is non-finite, <= 0, or not an integer, because a fractional size can never satisfy the receiver's exact-match completion gate (receivedSize === metaData.size over integer chunk byte lengths); humanFileSize clamps its unit index on both ends (Math.max(0, ...)) so a peer-controlled size in (0, 1) floors to unit 0 instead of indexing units[-1] to undefined.

The dead-channel onerror/onclose teardown that previously lived copy-pasted in OfferPage.svelte and ReceivePage.svelte is now the shared createChannelTeardown(options) factory in src/utils/channelTeardown.ts (PR #135, mirroring the channelSender.ts guarded-send and peerMessage.ts handler dedups: every dead-channel hardening since PR #74/#104 had to land on both pages in lockstep, and a future hardening on only one page would silently desync peer behavior). Both pages assign dataChannel.onerror/onclose to the helper's onerror ('WebRTC error' toast) and onclose ('Disconnected' toast). The helper is the single place that: toasts, resets the page's isConnecting via markNotConnecting(), runs the page-specific lost hook (OfferPage clears the dead generation's offerLink; ReceivePage passes none), propagates 'connection lost' into BOTH file pipelines via getSender()?.onChannelClose() / getReceiver()?.onChannelClose(), and releases the RTCPeerConnection guarded on connectionState !== 'closed' (closing the data channel alone leaves the ICE agent, UDP sockets, and STUN/TURN keepalives live; close() throws InvalidStateError on an already-closed peer, which an error+close double-fire or a racing regeneration would otherwise surface). The getConnection option must read the CURRENT RTCPeerConnection at fire time, not a captured one: the offer page reassigns its connection to a new peer on every regeneration, so a handler that survives a regeneration race must close the peer that actually owns the dying generation (ReceivePage's connection is a const, so a plain getter covers it too). Pinned by tests/channel-teardown.test.mjs and tests/dead-channel-peer-close.test.mjs.

The static build must stay base-relative so a sub-path deployment (an org GitHub Pages site or a self-hosted base) does not 404 its own assets: PR #138 made the PWA manifest use a relative start_url ('.') and relative icon paths ('./pwa-192x192.png', './pwa-512x512.png') instead of site-root-absolute '/…' (which would resolve to the deployment root and 404 under a sub-path), and main.astro derives the favicon.ico and manifest.webmanifest links and the og:image from Vite's import.meta.env.BASE_URL — the og:image is absolutized against the configured Astro.site origin when present, else left base-prefixed for scrapers to resolve against the page URL (replacing the earlier hardcoded canonical-domain og:image). tests/subpath-static-references.test.mjs (PR #138/#139) pins the whole class: the layout's static references, the manifest's relative start_url/icons, the service-worker registration path auto-injected by astrojs-service-worker (base-prefixed <base>/service-worker.js), and the emitted service-worker.js's relative-only precache URLs — a root-absolute registration or precache URL would 404 against the <base>/ service-worker scope.

The per-file progress + bitrate UI-update block that previously lived copy-pasted in Sender.svelte (sendNextChunk) and Receiver.svelte (processChunk) is now the shared updateTransferProgress(stats, sentBytes, totalBytes, writeTo) helper in src/utils/transferProgress.ts (PR #136, mirroring the channelSender.ts/peerMessage.ts/channelTeardown.ts dedups): pure math + state writes only (no toasts, no channel sends — the surrounding chunk-slicing/ack/blob/reject pipeline stays in the components). It clamps progress to [0,100] with a NaN→0 fallback (uniform for both sides), computes bitrate = sentBytes/elapsed where elapsed is time-since-ACCEPT (stats.startTime) floored to a 1 ms minimum — a small file whose accept and first progress update share a millisecond makes the raw denominator 0, and bytes/0 is Infinity, a value that would be stored in $state and render as a misleading '0 B/sec' (PR #134) — and advances nextProgressUpdate by PROGRESS_UPDATE_UI_STEP clamped to 100. The receiver passes receivingFileStatsMap[id] as the stats argument, so its bitrate denominator reads the stats clock (receivingFileStatsMap[id].startTime, the onAccept-time clock initialized in onAccept); the helper reads stats.startTime regardless of call site, keeping the two call sites byte-identical. Pinned by tests/transfer-progress.test.mjs and tests/bitrate-zero-elapsed-guard.test.mjs.
